label: input token a (fed back during copy, or at t=0)
explanation: Fires when the input token is the letter a, almost entirely in the copy phase (a fed back as the model own output; ~95% of activation mass, typical activation 0.65-1.0 of max). It also fires weakly (~0.17 of max) when a is the very first original token (t=0). It does NOT fire on a in original positions t>=1 (except a few weak hits), never at the delimiter step, and essentially never on other tokens. Magnitude is highest for the first a of a repeated aa run in the copy phase (~1.0) and somewhat lower for the second a (~0.75-0.85); the t=0 case is the weakest. Predicate precision is 1.0 on dev; misses are a few weak original-phase a activations at t=1..2.

issues: Minor overclaim: the explanation says the second a in a copy-phase 'aa' run fires at about 0.75-0.85 against about 1.0 for the first. Measured on test, mean activation per step is 1.005e-5 for a with prev_tok==a (mass 0.0247 over 2462 steps) and 1.044e-5 for a with prev_tok!=a (mass 0.928 over 88879 steps). That ratio is about 0.96, so the second a is at most slightly weaker. The claimed drop comes from a few top examples and does not hold on average.

The t=1 case is understated. When a is the input at t=1 the feature fires 16% of the time (precision 0.163, 16652 predicted steps), which is a regular weak pattern rather than 'a few hits'. It holds only 0.4% of the mass, though. For original a at t>=2 the firing rate is 1% (mass 0.13%), so 'does not fire' holds there.

Test misses (5531 steps, 0.9% of mass) are scattered weak activations of about 0.10-0.14. Most are original a at t=1, plus a weak echo on the copy-phase token just before an a is fed back (rel_tok(1)==a in copy has precision 0.05). Neither is a material systematic gap.

These claims check out: no false positives on test (precision 1.0), no firing at the delimiter step, about 95.5% of mass in the copy phase, the t=0 case weak at about 0.18 of max (t=0 a: precision 1.0, mass recall 0.038 over 16.5k steps), and almost no firing on non-a copy-phase inputs (precision 0.0008).
